doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

title: Music schools: scholarship, going where the food is, New School teachers
summary: Glasper says school got him out of Houston churches; teachers like Reggie Workman and Charlie Persip played with the greats.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So we went into some kind of musical depth into your history. Here I’d like to direct it for the students here and the students looking. Some of the questions that I ask will be kind of directed towards them and where they’re at. All right. So the first question I have for you has to do with the fact that you have a very identifiable voice and style as a band leader, as a performer, as a musician, even as a composer. And I’d like you to talk about the importance of an individual voice. Because you know in the music’s history, that was like the thing. That used to be the thing. It’s like you’ve got to have it, your voice.

But in music schools when you have, instead of it being on the bandstand and through traveling on the road with big bands and that type of thing where it was an apprenticeship process, now that you have a lot of music schools it seems to be more of a — not a

cookie cutter, but less — maybe cookie cutter. Maybe less of the individuality. So could you talk about that? Because I think the young people here, they — I think they need to hear about the importance of that.

Yeah, totally. It’s — the music in schools is good and bad, you know what I mean? For the most part it’s good because if there wasn’t music in schools I wouldn’t be sitting here, you know, I’d be somewhere in Houston at somebody’s church, playing in church, being that cat that’s really good in Houston, you know? But I was able to get a full scholarship to go to college, to go up to New York, you know. So that’s why, I made it there. I mean Miles Davis went to music school. I mean that’s the good thing about school. It gets you where you need to be. You know like some people don’t get ahead in life simply because of where they are.

Because of the geographical thing, not because of a talent thing or anything like that. They’re just not — you’ve got to move where the food is or else you’re going to be hungry. It’s simple. You know so many people have said that, like, “I’m hungry.” And I’m like, “you need to go where the food is.” You know? And then they don’t want to take the sacrifice to do it and it can be hard. But luckily if there’s school it takes some of that padding out, it makes it less hard, because of school. And then when you’re grown it’s like move to New York and you have nothing. Then it’s like a little bit harder because now where are you going to live, there’s no dormitory and nothing like that. You’re grown now so it’s a little harder. But for me school was the thing. And, you know, a lot of times with schools, you know you have teachers in the schools, most of the time, that, a lot of them are sometimes failed musicians and you know what I mean? They can teach but they can’t teach you how to be yourself. You know what I mean? Some schools have great teachers like that. New School had great teachers like that. They actually have teachers that were on amazing records. Like one of my teachers was Reggie Workman. You know? What else do you need?

Right. Charlie Persip, you know? I had cats teaching me that played with Bird. You know what I mean? So that’s a different thing. Because they were around all those individual cats and they understand the thing. They’re not failed musicians or anything, they’re in schools because they want to teach us, give us what they know. Not because that’s all they got. And so before music became a music business per se, it was really cool to be yourself and have your own voice. And that’s what it was about. Who’s different? That’s why so many different groups and even individual artists, you’re looking in the 60s or 70s and the 80s, there were so many different kinds of artists looking different, sounding different, the music was different, blah-blah-blah, and everybody can make it.
